{"markdown":"# Issues Memo — Master Services Agreement

**To:** Deal team  
**From:** In-house counsel (Customer side)  
**Re:** Playbook review of the Vendor's Master Services Agreement

---

## 1. Executive summary

We have completed our playbook review of the Master Services Agreement. The draft is, on the whole, strongly favourable to us: intellectual property, indemnification, licence scope, assignment and change of control, termination for convenience, transition assistance, audit rights, renewal mechanics, warranties, insurance and governing law all meet our preferred positions, and the agreement imposes no exclusivity, non-compete, non-solicit, minimum-commitment or most-favoured-customer burden on us.

Two issues require negotiation, and one of them is a walk-away item:

1. **Limitation of liability cap basis (§ 21) — critical.** The cap is mutual and the Excluded Claims set matches our preferred carve-outs, but the cap base is illusory. "Fees" is defined in §§ 1.5/1.6 as only the one-time USD 12,000 Implementation Fee under the first Order Form, so the ceiling sits far below six months' actual spend. As drafted this is walk-away territory.
2. **Customer-payable liquidated damages (§ 7.7) — high.** Liquidated damages accrue against us weekly at 15% of annual Fees on a ten-day payment delay. This is a penalty running against us and falls outside even our fallback (a single early-termination fee capped at three months' fees).

We recommend tabling both points together, with the cap basis as the priority.

---

## 2. Findings

| Severity | Rule | Status | Section |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Critical | LOL-CAP — Limitation of liability: cap, mutuality and carve-outs | **Deviation** | § 21 Limitation of Liability |
| Critical | INDEMN — Indemnification by Vendor | Compliant | § 20 Indemnification |
| Critical | IP — Ownership of deliverables and Customer Data | Compliant | § 14 Intellectual Property and Deliverables |
| High | LD — Liquidated damages and penalties payable by Customer | **Deviation** | § 7 Fees, Invoicing, and Taxes (§ 7.7) |
| High | ASSIGN — Assignment and change of control | Compliant | § 24 Assignment and Change of Control |
| High | EXCLUSIVITY — Exclusivity obligations binding Customer | Compliant | § 2 Agreement Structure and Scope |
| High | LICENSE — Licence grant scope | Compliant | § 13 Access Rights and Licence |
| High | NONCOMPETE — Non-compete restrictions on Customer | Compliant | § 12 Customer Responsibilities |
| High | T4C — Termination for convenience | Compliant | § 9 Termination (with § 29.4) |
| Medium | AUDIT — Audit rights against Customer | Compliant | § 22 Audit Rights |
| Medium | GOVLAW — Governing law and venue | Compliant | § 28 Governing Law and Dispute Resolution |
| Medium | MFN — Most-favoured-nation obligations burdening Customer | Compliant | § 7 Fees, Invoicing, and Taxes |
| Medium | MINCOMMIT — Minimum purchase commitments and volume restrictions | Compliant | § 2 Agreement Structure and Scope |
| Medium | NOSOLICIT — Non-solicitation of employees binding Customer | Compliant | § 12 Customer Responsibilities |
| Medium | RENEWAL — Auto-renewal and non-renewal notice window | Compliant | § 8 Term and Renewal |
| Medium | TRANSITION — Post-termination transition assistance and data return | Compliant | § 11 Transition Assistance and Data Return |
| Medium | WARRANTY — Performance warranty and duration | Compliant | § 19 Warranties |
| Low | INSURANCE — Vendor insurance | Compliant | § 18 Insurance |

### Detail on the two deviations

**§ 21 — Limitation of liability (critical).** The cap is mutual, indirect damages are mutually excluded, and § 21.3 carves out Excluded Claims consistent with our preferred position (including confirmation that payment obligations are not damages). The defect is the cap base: because "Fees" is defined in §§ 1.5/1.6 as only the one-time USD 12,000 Implementation Fee under the first Order Form, the ceiling is far below six months' actual spend. **Our redline:** measure the cap on the greater of (a) all amounts paid or payable in the preceding twelve months and (b) USD 1,000,000.

**§ 7.7 — Liquidated damages payable by Customer (high).** Liquidated damages accrue weekly at 15% of annual Fees on a ten-day delay. **Our redline:** delete the customer-payable liquidated damages for late payment and replace them with customary simple late interest on undisputed amounts.

---

## 3. Walk-away items

- **Liability cap measured on the USD 12,000 Implementation Fee (§ 21, read with §§ 1.5/1.6).** An illusory cap base is walk-away territory under our playbook. We cannot sign on a ceiling set far below six months' actual spend; the cap must be reset to the greater of twelve months' amounts paid or payable and USD 1,000,000.

---

## 4. Next steps

1. Issue our redline on § 21 (cap basis) and § 7.7 (liquidated damages to late interest), with short rationale comments carrying the `[Playbook]` prefix.
2. Flag to the business that the § 21 cap basis is a walk-away item so that escalation authority is clear before the next call.
3. Confirm with finance the expected annual spend under the initial and anticipated Order Forms, so we can validate that the twelve-month/USD 1,000,000 formulation is adequate.
4. Accept the remaining sections as drafted; no further redlines are required, and we should preserve the Vendor-granted MFN in § 7, the Vendor-side restraint in § 12.4 and the transition terms in § 11, each of which runs in our favour.
"}
